entries.04857d49067b2ea6: The business designs, builds and operates facilities for treating solid waste such as refuse incineration. The main products listed in the securities report are municipal waste incineration plants, industrial waste incineration plants and water treatment plants, and the company provides engineering and construction work for design, procurement and construction (EPC), as well as plant operation management and maintenance (O&M). The business is carried out by Ebara Environmental Plant Co., Ltd., Ebara Environmental Engineering (China) Co., Ltd., and the equity-method joint-controlled company Suidō Ing Co., Ltd., in which the company holds 33.3% of the voting rights; Suidō Ing Co., Ltd. also manufactures and sells chemicals in addition to operation and maintenance. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥97,864 million (¥87,438 million in the previous fiscal year, an 11.9% increase year on year), and segment profit was ¥13,003 million (¥8,445 million in the previous fiscal year, a 54.0% increase year on year). Orders received were ¥135,392 million (¥71,594 million in the previous fiscal year, an 89.1% increase year on year), order backlog was ¥384,675 million, and the number of employees was 2,830. The company cites as reasons for the increase in revenue the receipt of four large-scale orders for life extension and renovation of waste treatment facilities, an increase in O&M, and an improvement in profitability.

entries.3ffcccd91ce4184d: What is sold differs by the buyer's field. Building & Industrial covers standard pumps (land, submersible and water supply), refrigeration machinery and blowers, for building and industrial facilities. Energy covers custom pumps, compressors, turbines, cryopumps and expanders, for oil and gas, power and new energy. Infrastructure covers custom pumps for agricultural, drainage, and water and sewage use, and tunnel blowers, for water infrastructure. Environment covers municipal waste incineration plants, industrial waste incineration plants and water treatment plants, and in addition to engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) work, it also performs operation management and maintenance (O&M). Precision & Electronics covers vacuum pumps, CMP equipment, plating equipment and exhaust gas treatment equipment, for semiconductor manufacturing. After-sales service (called 'Service & Support' in the report) appears many times in explanations of order and sales trends in domestic Building & Industrial, Energy, and Precision & Electronics. As a common policy across the business, the report states that it aims to become a 'solutions provider' that collects and analyzes operating data from products delivered to customers and offers services such as energy saving, predictive failure management and operation guarantees. Consolidated R&D expenses were ¥23,233 million, of which Precision & Electronics had the largest share at ¥12,009 million among the five companies, and the company-wide technology policy lists fluid analysis and control, vibration and noise control, and interface control as core technologies. In November 2025, it entered into an agreement to acquire, among others, the three-phase motor and IPM motor business of [[company:mitsubishi-electric|Mitsubishi Electric Corporation]]. The transfer date is 'during fiscal 2026 (planned),' and as of the report, the transfer has not been completed.

entries.5266f23130e94618: The business supplies machinery for the oil and gas, power and new energy sectors. The main products listed in the securities report are custom pumps, compressors, turbines, cryopumps and expanders. Manufacturing, sales and maintenance are handled by the company itself, together with EBARA ELLIOTT SERVICES, INC. in Japan, and overseas by Elliott Company (United States), Jialite Ebara Pump Industry Co., Ltd. and Ebara Machinery Zibo Co., Ltd. (China), and Elliott Ebara Singapore Pte. Ltd. (Singapore). Elliott Company is separately disclosed by the securities report with its main profit and loss information, as it accounts for more than 10% of consolidated revenue excluding internal transactions (revenue including internal transactions was ¥130,438 million). Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥217,845 million (¥210,434 million in the previous fiscal year, a 3.5% increase year on year), the third largest after Building & Industrial. Segment profit, on the other hand, was ¥25,943 million (¥28,008 million in the previous fiscal year, a 7.4% decrease year on year), with profit falling mainly due to an increase in fixed costs. Orders received were ¥194,777 million (¥222,743 million in the previous fiscal year, a 12.6% decrease year on year), order backlog was ¥213,790 million, and the number of employees was 3,585. The company explains that orders fell below the previous year due to a decline in petrochemical projects and reduced field services and parts, while revenue increased because Service & Support was solid in the Middle East and Asia.

entries.5651b2c38dae66bd: EBARA CORPORATION makes and sells pumps, blowers, refrigeration and heating equipment, compressors and turbines, semiconductor manufacturing equipment, waste incineration plants and more, and also handles maintenance and operation management after sale. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] (hereafter, the report) divides its businesses into 5 Companies by buyer field (called "facing markets" in the report's terms): "Building and Industry", "Energy", "Infrastructure", "Environment" and "Precision and Electronics", and states that this division is the same as the reportable [[term:segment|segments]]. There are 2 main ways in which it recognizes revenue. The 1st is to recognize revenue when products such as pumps and equipment are delivered to the customer (or accepted by the customer). The other 1, as with construction contracts and maintenance contracts, is to recognize revenue according to progress over the period of the construction or maintenance, and the report states that progress is measured by "the ratio of actual costs to total estimated costs". Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥958,285 million and orders received were ¥949,683 million, and the order backlog as of December 31, 2025 was ¥912,020 million. By reportable segment, the order backlog was ¥384,675 million for Environment, ¥213,790 million for Energy, ¥151,591 million for Precision and Electronics, ¥83,453 million for Infrastructure and ¥75,789 million for Building and Industry, with Environment the largest. In Note 28, the report presents the same amount as the backlog as "unsatisfied performance obligations", and states that these mainly belong to custom pumps, compressors and turbines (Building and Industry, Energy, Infrastructure) and long-term comprehensive contracts in Environment, and that many are long-term construction contracts exceeding 1 year. The period over which Environment is expected to be recognized as revenue is within 20 years.

entries.6112afcaac29e882: The business supplies pumps for water infrastructure (water-related facilities that support society). The main products listed in the securities report are custom pumps (agricultural pumps, drainage pumps, sewage and water supply pumps) and tunnel blowers; manufacturing, sales, operation and maintenance are handled by the company itself and Ebara Densan Ltd. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥57,143 million (¥51,118 million in the previous fiscal year, an 11.8% increase year on year), the smallest of the five reportable segments. Segment profit was ¥4,680 million (¥3,697 million in the previous fiscal year, a 26.6% increase year on year), orders received were ¥62,973 million (a 4.0% increase year on year), order backlog was ¥83,453 million, and the number of employees was 1,581. The company cites solid demand for renewal and repair in the domestic public pump market, large-scale orders received in South America and North America overseas, and steady progress in working off the order backlog.

entries.84285466249d301e: EBARA CORPORATION, headquartered at 11-1 Haneda Asahi-cho, Ota-ku, Tokyo, together with 108 subsidiaries (of which 108 are [[term:consolidated-subsidiary|consolidated subsidiaries]]), three associates and one joint venture, make up the group. The number of employees as of December 31, 2025 was 21,148 (number of persons employed). The organization is made up of five companies, and revenue from external customers by reportable segment is, in order, ¥342,267 million for Precision & Electronics, ¥241,938 million for Building & Industrial, ¥217,845 million for Energy, ¥97,864 million for Environment, and ¥57,143 million for Infrastructure. In addition, 'Other,' not included in reportable segments (such as regional headquarters companies in China), amounts to ¥1,225 million. Accounts are prepared under [[term:ifrs|International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)]], and the fiscal year-end is December. In Environment, Suiing Co., Ltd. (a joint venture accounted for under the equity method, with 33.3% of voting rights) handles operation and maintenance and the manufacture and sale of chemicals, and is treated separately from Ebara's consolidated subsidiaries.
entries.8a628750b78e5844: Revenue for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥958,285 million, up 10.6% from ¥866,668 million in the previous fiscal year. The securities report’s revenue recognition policy states that revenue from manufacturing and selling products is mainly recognized at the time of delivery or acceptance of the products. Construction contracts and maintenance contracts in Building & Industry, Energy, Infrastructure and Environment are recognized as revenue over the period of construction or maintenance, according to progress, if any of certain requirements are met. Progress is measured as the ratio of actual costs to estimated total costs. For Precision & Electronics, the securities report describes only the manufacture and sale of products (at delivery or acceptance) as its revenue recognition method and does not describe the treatment of maintenance services. As of December 31, 2025, receivables arising from contracts with customers were ¥207,582 million, contract assets recognized according to construction progress were ¥119,684 million, and contract liabilities, which are consideration received from customers for performance obligations not yet fulfilled, were ¥82,498 million (at the end of the previous fiscal year: ¥167,850 million, ¥116,792 million and ¥108,778 million, respectively). The same amount as the total order backlog of ¥912,020 million is printed in Note 28 as “transaction price allocated to unsatisfied performance obligations.” The securities report states that these performance obligations are expected to be completed and recognized as revenue mostly within three years for Building & Industry, Energy and Infrastructure, within 20 years for Environment, and within one year for Precision & Electronics.

entries.bbd56090ac51e6ab: A business providing equipment and components for factories that make semiconductors, and the largest segment at Ebara. The main products listed in the securities report are vacuum pumps, CMP equipment (equipment that polishes and flattens the surface of a [[term:wafer|wafer]]), plating equipment and exhaust gas treatment equipment, and the main end market (customer field) is semiconductor manufacturing. The company handles manufacturing and sales, while Ebara Field Tech Co., Ltd., Ebara Technologies Inc., Shanghai Ebara Precision Machinery Co., Ltd., Ebara Precision Machinery Korea Inc., Taiwan Ebara Precision Machinery Co., Ltd., and Ebara Precision Machinery Europe GmbH handle sales and after-sales service. Production and development of [[term:semiconductor-manufacturing-equipment|semiconductor manufacturing equipment]] and vacuum pumps are handled at the Fujisawa Business Site in Kanagawa Prefecture, and production of semiconductor manufacturing equipment is handled at the Kumamoto Business Site in Kumamoto Prefecture. In the fiscal year ended December 2025, external customer revenue was ¥342,267 million (prior year ¥278,378 million, up 23.0% year on year), the largest of the 5 reportable segments. Segment profit was ¥57,773 million (prior year ¥50,133 million), orders received were ¥303,447 million (up 16.7% year on year), and the number of employees was 4,000. The company explains that demand for CMP and components recovered, and that both products and service & support exceeded the previous year. The filing also states that while customers' factory utilization rates continue to recover, centered on demand for generative AI, the full-scale resumption of capacity-expansion investment is later than initially expected.
entries.bca34f6b0d62124c: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥113,802 million (previous year: ¥97,953 million, up 16.2%), and profit attributable to owners of the parent was ¥76,633 million (previous year: ¥71,401 million, up 7.3%); the securities report states that orders received, revenue, operating profit and profit each reached record highs. Segment profit (on an operating profit basis) was ¥57,773 million for Precision & Electronics, ¥25,943 million for Energy, ¥15,251 million for Building & Industry, ¥13,003 million for Environment and ¥4,680 million for Infrastructure, while “Others,” which is not included in reportable segments, recorded a loss of ¥2,294 million. Precision & Electronics, the largest segment by revenue, is also the largest by profit. The reasons for the increase in profit given by the company are: revenue rose in Precision & Electronics and Infrastructure; in Environment, revenue rose and profitability improved; and in Building & Industry, the goodwill impairment loss related to Vansan in Turkey that was recorded in the previous year no longer occurred. Only Energy recorded a decrease in profit, which the company mainly attributes to an increase in fixed costs.
entries.bcb26c7062b91b6c: The business supplies pumps and air-conditioning and cooling machinery used in building equipment and industrial facilities. The main products listed in the securities report are standard pumps (land pumps, submersible pumps, water supply pumps), refrigeration and heat-related machinery, and blowers. Manufacturing, sales and maintenance are handled by the company itself, together with EBARA REFRIGERATION & AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEMS, INC. and EBARA WIND ENERGY MACHINERY, INC. in Japan, and overseas by EBARA BOMBAS AMÉRICA DO SUL LTDA. (Brazil), Ebara Pumps Europe S.p.A. (Italy), EBARA PUMPS IBERIA, S.A. (Spain), Ebara Refrigeration & Air Conditioning Systems (China) Co., Ltd. and Ebara Machinery (China) Co., Ltd. (China), Ebara Engineering Singapore Pte. Ltd. (Singapore), Vansan Makina Sanayi ve Ticaret A.S. (Turkey), and EBARA HG Holdings Inc. and EBARA PUMPS AMERICAS CORPORATION (United States). Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended December 2025 was ¥241,938 million (¥238,182 million in the previous fiscal year, a 1.6% increase year on year), the second largest after Precision & Electronics. Segment profit was ¥15,251 million (¥10,341 million in the previous fiscal year), and orders received were ¥249,285 million (a 2.0% increase year on year); with 7,654 employees, it has the largest workforce of the five reportable segments. The company explains that in Japan, Service & Support performed well, and overseas, China was weak while North America's data center demand and the Middle East and Europe were solid. The company also cites the absence of the goodwill impairment loss recorded in the previous year related to Vansan (consolidated goodwill impairment loss of ¥7,085 million) as a reason for the increase in profit.
